domain_label: Turlock & Central Valley Wage-Job Income Ladder
purpose: A session-bounded method for raising a worker's earned income from W-2 wage jobs in Turlock and Stanislaus County by inventorying constraints, mapping local sectors and pay bands from EDD/BLS OEWS data, choosing low-barrier entry and short-credential upgrades by ROI, exploiting shift and overtime premiums, working real hiring channels, and committing to a dated reassessment loop.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all pay bands and scores are reasoned heuristic priors, not quotes
the worker is legally able to accept W-2 employment in the United States and can complete Form I-9
the geography is Turlock / Stanislaus County within the Modesto MSA labor market in 2026
the worker has at least intermittent transport and a phone reachable for employer callbacks
pay figures are reasoned local bands keyed to EDD/BLS OEWS Modesto MSA wage structure, not employer quotes
exclusions: commercial-driving credentials (CDL Class A/B and the driving career ladder) — covered by a separate KB
starting or operating a business, franchising, or self-employed trade contracting — covered by a separate KB
1099 gig income as a primary strategy beyond a short W-2-vs-1099 comparison node
immigration legal advice or how to obtain work authorization documents one does not have
relocation outside Stanislaus County and the immediate Modesto MSA
source_description: heuristic prior estimates for Central Valley wage-job income work units, informed by EDD Labor Market Information, BLS OEWS Modesto MSA occupational wage structure, California wage-and-hour law, and general knowledge of Stanislaus County employers and hiring channels; no supplied dataset
source_citation: California EDD Labor Market Information Division, Modesto MSA occupational employment & wage data; U.S. BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OEWS); USCIS Form I-9 Lists of Acceptable Documents; California Labor Code (overtime, meal/rest, agricultural overtime AB 1066); CalJOBS / America's Job Center of California (Stanislaus); heuristic priors where no dataset is supplied

competency_questions.question: What are the worker's current skills, documents, available hours, transport, and hard constraints, and how do they bound the reachable job set?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SELF_INVENTORY records skills, I-9 document readiness, weekly hour window, transport radius, and disqualifiers; CONSTRAINT_MODEL converts them into an explicit reachable/blocked job filter

competency_questions.question: Which sectors and employer types dominate Turlock/Stanislaus wage employment, and which structurally pay more?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SECTOR_MAP names the dominant local sectors and example employer types; PAY_BANDS attaches reasoned OEWS-keyed wage bands and identifies the higher-paying ones

competency_questions.question: How are realistic local pay bands estimated without quoting employers, and what method anchors them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PAY_BANDS states the EDD/BLS OEWS Modesto MSA method and gives reasoned low/median/high bands per role family

competency_questions.question: What is the fastest low-barrier way to start earning a wage now given the worker's constraints?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FAST_ENTRY identifies entry roles requiring no credential and the channel that fills them quickest, consistent with CONSTRAINT_MODEL

competency_questions.question: Which higher-wage roles are reachable with only short training, and is the credential's ROI positive?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SHORT_CREDENTIALS lists short certs reachable in weeks and CREDENTIAL_ROI computes the wage delta against time and cost to confirm payback

competency_questions.question: How can shift, overtime, and seasonal-peak premiums raise total pay on the same base wage?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SHIFT_PREMIUMS quantifies night/weekend differentials, daily/weekly overtime, and seasonal pack-house peak hours under California rules

competency_questions.question: What are the real hiring channels and the minimal effective application to reach them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HIRING_CHANNELS ranks referral, staffing/temp-to-hire, CalJOBS/county job center, and walk-in; APPLICATION_MIN specifies the minimal resume/contact packet

competency_questions.question: What pre-hire screening should the worker expect and prepare for?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCREENING_PREP enumerates drug test, background check, physical/lift test, and forklift certification and how to prepare for each

competency_questions.question: Which work-authorization documents satisfy Form I-9 and how should they be assembled before applying?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WORK_AUTH_DOCS maps List A vs List B+C document combinations and confirms the worker can present a valid set on day one

competency_questions.question: What internal promotion ladders, skill-stacking certs, and union/public-sector/apprenticeship routes raise wages over months?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROMOTION_LADDER describes internal lead/operator steps and skill-stacking; UNION_PUBLIC_ROUTES covers union, county/city, and apprenticeship pathways

competency_questions.question: How does total compensation differ from the headline wage, and how do W-2 and 1099 offers compare?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TOTAL_COMP separates headline wage from benefits, taxes, and reimbursed costs and contrasts W-2 with 1099 net pay

competency_questions.question: How are dead-end, exploitative, and scam wage offers detected and avoided?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCAM_FILTER lists red flags (pay-to-work, cash-only wage theft, fake staffing, no I-9) and a go/no-go rule

competency_questions.question: How is a dated 6-12 month income plan built and sequenced from the reachable options?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INCOME_PLAN produces a dated sequence: earn-now job, short credential, premium-shift move, and promotion target with milestone dates

competency_questions.question: When and how is the plan reassessed, and what triggers a re-inventory?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REASSESS_LOOP defines the cadence and the material-change triggers that send the worker back through SELF_INVENTORY and PAY_BANDS

glossary.definition: BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics: the survey program whose Modesto MSA tables give local 10th/median/90th-percentile hourly wages per occupation, used here to reason pay bands instead of quoting employers.
The Modesto Metropolitan Statistical Area, coextensive with Stanislaus County, which is the labor market that Turlock sits inside and the geography EDD/BLS wage data is reported for.

A staffing-agency arrangement where the worker is payrolled by the agency for a probationary period (often 90-520 hours) and, if retained, converted to the host employer's direct payroll, usually at a raise.
An added per-hour amount (commonly a fixed cents/hour or a percent) paid for swing, graveyard, or weekend shifts on top of the base wage, distinct from overtime.
On Form I-9, a single document (e.g., U.S. passport, Permanent Resident Card) that alone proves both identity and work authorization, removing the need for a List B + List C pair.

An OSHA-required operator evaluation (classroom plus a practical drive test on a specific truck class) that warehouses and pack houses treat as a quick wage-raising credential; it is employer- and equipment-specific.

Under California AB 1066, the phased rule giving most ag workers daily/weekly overtime, so that peak-season pack-house and field hours past the threshold pay at 1.5x, materially changing seasonal earnings.
The Stanislaus County one-stop career center and CalJOBS portal offering free job listings, resume help, WIOA-funded short training, and referrals to local employers.

The full value of a job beyond the headline hourly wage: employer-paid health/dental, retirement match, paid sick/vacation, shift premiums, and reimbursed costs minus the worker's payroll taxes and commute cost.
Accumulating several cheap, fast certifications (forklift, food-safety/ServSafe, basic GMP, first aid) so a worker qualifies for a higher pay band than any single cert would unlock.

nodes.definition: Take a structured inventory of the worker's transferable skills, work history, language and reading level, I-9 document readiness, weekly available hours and shift flexibility, transport radius, and any hard limits (childcare, health, schedule). This is the raw input that bounds every downstream job choice and must be honest rather than aspirational.

included: weekly hour window and shift tolerance

pros.claim: An honest hour-and-transport window prevents applying to jobs the worker cannot physically keep
pros.example: a worker with no graveyard childcare rules out the 11pm dairy sanitation shift before it wastes an interview

cons.claim: Self-assessment understates transferable skills, hiding qualifying experience
cons.example: a parent treats years of household budgeting as nothing when it reads as inventory/cash-handling experience

failure_modes: transport reliability overstated so the worker no-shows in week two
I-9 documents assumed available but actually expired or lost
acceptance_tests: the inventory names at least five transferable skills, a concrete weekly hour window, a transport radius in miles, and confirms which I-9 documents are physically in hand
revisit_triggers: childcare, health, or housing situation changes
the worker gains or loses reliable transport

base.update_signal: the worker's hours, transport, documents, or hard constraints are restated

nodes.definition: Map the sectors that actually dominate wage employment in Turlock and Stanislaus County — food and dairy processing, agriculture and pack houses, warehousing/logistics, healthcare, retail/grocery, education, and city/county public sector — and the example employer types in each. This grounds the search in real local demand rather than national job-board noise.

pros.claim: Targeting locally dominant sectors raises callback odds because those employers hire continuously
pros.example: almond and dairy processors run year-round lines and backfill turnover weekly, unlike a single distant warehouse

cons.claim: Over-weighting the biggest sectors can steer a worker into the most physically punishing, highest-turnover lines
cons.example: treating pack-house seasonal work as a career when it furloughs every winter

failure_modes: chasing a glamorous sector with almost no local headcount
ignoring public-sector openings because they post on a separate county portal
acceptance_tests: the map lists at least six local sectors with at least two concrete employer types each, drawn from Turlock/Stanislaus reality
revisit_triggers: a large local plant opens, closes, or announces layoffs
a new distribution center breaks ground in the county

base.update_signal: a major local employer opens, closes, or relocates

nodes.definition: Convert the raw inventory into an explicit filter: which jobs are reachable today, which are blocked, and what single change would unblock the most value. It intersects hour windows, transport radius, document status, and physical limits against the sector map so the search only spends effort on jobs the worker can actually take and keep.

pros.claim: Naming the one binding constraint shows the cheapest way to widen the job set
pros.example: a bus pass turns a 3-mile walking radius into a 12-mile reach covering three more processors

cons.claim: A constraint filter applied too rigidly discards jobs a small accommodation would have allowed
cons.example: ruling out all night shifts when one employer offers a fixed early-evening swing

failure_modes: filtering on an assumed constraint that is actually negotiable
leaving the binding constraint unidentified so effort scatters
acceptance_tests: the model outputs a reachable-job list, a blocked-job list with the reason each is blocked, and names the single highest-leverage unblocker
revisit_triggers: the worker resolves the previously binding constraint
a new constraint appears that shrinks the reachable set

base.update_signal: a constraint is resolved or a new one appears

nodes.definition: Confirm the worker can present a valid Form I-9 document set on day one: either a single List A document (U.S. passport, Permanent Resident Card, or employment authorization document) or a List B identity document plus a List C work-authorization document (e.g., driver's license plus unrestricted Social Security card or birth certificate). Missing or expired documents are the most common silent disqualifier and must be fixed before applying.

included: List A vs List B+C combinations
excluded: obtaining authorization the worker does not have

pros.claim: Assembling a valid I-9 set before applying removes the most common day-one rejection
pros.example: replacing a lost Social Security card a week early so a List B+C pair is ready at onboarding

cons.claim: Chasing the 'perfect' List A document can delay starting when a B+C pair already in hand would suffice
cons.example: waiting weeks for a passport when a license plus birth certificate already qualifies

failure_modes: showing up with an expired EAD that no longer authorizes work
presenting a restricted Social Security card that fails List C
acceptance_tests: the worker has a complete, unexpired List A document OR a valid List B + List C pair physically in hand before applying
revisit_triggers: a document expires or is lost
an employment authorization category or expiry date changes

base.update_signal: a work-authorization document is obtained, lost, or expires

nodes.definition: Estimate realistic low/median/high hourly bands for each local role family using the EDD/BLS OEWS Modesto MSA wage structure as the anchor, and flag which jobs structurally pay more. The method is to reason from the published percentile wages for the occupation in this MSA, not to quote any single employer; healthcare technical roles, skilled maintenance/mechanics, and licensed/public-sector roles sit above general production, retail, and entry warehousing.

included: OEWS-keyed low/median/high bands per role family

pros.claim: Anchoring to OEWS percentiles gives a defensible band without trusting a single inflated or lowball posting
pros.example: reading a production-worker median near the MSA entry band tells the worker a posted 'up to' figure is the rare 90th percentile

cons.claim: OEWS is a lagged annual survey, so fast-moving local raises (warehouse bidding wars) are understated
cons.example: a new fulfillment center paying above the table because it opened after the survey period

failure_modes: treating the 90th-percentile figure as a typical starting wage
comparing roles across MSAs and importing a coastal band into Turlock
acceptance_tests: each major role family has a reasoned low/median/high hourly band tied to the OEWS Modesto MSA method, and the higher-paying families are explicitly identified
revisit_triggers: a new OEWS release or EDD update lands
a local minimum-wage or industry-wage change takes effect

base.update_signal: a new OEWS/EDD wage release or wage-floor change occurs

nodes.definition: Establish the legal pay floor and rights every California wage job must honor: state minimum wage above the federal floor, mandated paid meal and rest breaks, accrued paid sick leave, final-pay timing, and the wage-theft recourse available through the Labor Commissioner. Knowing the floor lets a worker spot underpayment and refuse jobs that quietly violate it.

included: state minimum wage and break/sick-leave rights

pros.claim: Knowing the legal floor lets a worker recognize underpayment that a desperate applicant would accept
pros.example: spotting that off-the-clock pre-shift sanitation time must be paid and is not optional

cons.claim: Asserting every right aggressively at a new job can mark a worker as difficult before probation ends
cons.example: filing a complaint over a one-time short break instead of raising it informally first

failure_modes: accepting unpaid pre/post-shift work as normal
not knowing final pay is due promptly on separation
acceptance_tests: the worker can state the current state minimum wage, their break and paid-sick-leave entitlement, and the wage-theft recourse channel
revisit_triggers: the state or local minimum wage changes
a break, sick-leave, or final-pay law is amended

base.update_signal: a wage-floor, break, sick-leave, or wage-theft law changes

nodes.definition: Identify the fastest no-credential way to start earning now within the worker's reachable set: general production/line work, warehouse picking, grocery/retail stocking, dishwashing/food service, and seasonal pack-house labor, filled through staffing agencies and walk-ins that can place someone within days. This stops the bleed of zero income while longer plays develop.

included: fastest channel to a first paycheck

pros.claim: A same-week staffing placement converts idle time into wages and recent-work history
pros.example: a temp agency seats a worker on a packaging line Monday after a Thursday application

cons.claim: Low-barrier entry can become a trap if the worker stops climbing once income merely stabilizes
cons.example: staying three years on the same entry line at the same wage with no skill added

failure_modes: taking the first offer without checking it is not a scam or wage-theft setup
accepting a role whose shift the constraint model already flagged as unkeepable
acceptance_tests: at least three no-credential reachable roles are named with the specific channel that can place the worker within one to two weeks
revisit_triggers: the worker secures stable bridge income
a faster or better-paying entry channel opens

base.update_signal: the worker's immediate income need or fastest available channel changes

nodes.definition: Catalog the higher-wage roles reachable with only days-to-weeks of training: forklift/sit-down and reach certification, food-safety/ServSafe and GMP for processing leads, CNA/phlebotomy/medical-assistant short programs for healthcare, basic maintenance/mechanic entry, and WIOA-funded short courses through the county job center. Each is a small, fast investment that moves the worker up a pay band.

included: certs achievable in days to weeks

pros.claim: A weekend forklift cert can jump a worker from general labor into a warehouse operator band immediately
pros.example: an entry stocker certifies on a reach truck and moves up a pay grade within the same building

cons.claim: Some certs are employer- or equipment-specific and do not transfer, so paid-for training can strand value
cons.example: a private forklift card a host employer re-tests anyway, wasting the fee

failure_modes: paying a private school for a cert the county would fund free via WIOA
training for a role with no local demand
acceptance_tests: at least four short credentials are listed, each with its training time, rough cost or funding source, and the local role it unlocks
revisit_triggers: a WIOA-funded cohort opens or closes
an employer changes which certs it accepts

base.update_signal: a short-training option's cost, funding, or unlocked role changes

nodes.definition: Compute whether a short credential pays back: the hourly wage delta times expected annual hours, against the cost (tuition or zero if WIOA-funded), the unpaid training hours, and any forgone wages during training. A credential clears the bar when payback is a few weeks to a couple of months and the unlocked role has steady local demand.

included: wage-delta vs cost and time payback

pros.claim: An explicit payback period stops the worker from over-investing in a low-yield certificate
pros.example: a $0 WIOA forklift cert paying back in two weeks beats a $1,200 private one paying back in four months

cons.claim: ROI math on a single role ignores option value — a cert that opens several future ladders
cons.example: food-safety training that looks marginal alone but is the gate to every lead role

failure_modes: counting the wage delta but ignoring forgone wages during unpaid training
assuming full-time hours for a seasonal role
acceptance_tests: each candidate credential has a computed payback period and a go/no-go verdict tied to local demand durability
revisit_triggers: the wage delta or cost assumption changes
the unlocked role's local demand shifts

base.update_signal: the cost, wage delta, or hours assumption behind a credential changes

nodes.definition: Quantify how to raise total pay on the same base wage through California-rule premiums: night/swing/weekend shift differentials, daily overtime past eight hours and double-time past twelve, weekly overtime past forty, and seasonal pack-house peak hours where agricultural overtime under AB 1066 applies. Choosing a premium-rich shift can outearn a higher base on a day shift.

pros.claim: A graveyard differential plus daily overtime can lift effective pay well above a higher day-shift base
pros.example: a swing-shift line worker with a differential and ten-hour days outearns a day worker at a higher posted base

cons.claim: Premium-rich shifts trade money for health, sleep, and family time, raising burnout and turnover risk
cons.example: rotating graveyards that erode the worker's reliability within months

failure_modes: assuming overtime is guaranteed when it is discretionary and seasonal
missing that some employers cap hours to avoid overtime
acceptance_tests: the analysis states the differential, daily/weekly overtime, and seasonal-peak rules and shows an effective-pay comparison of a premium shift vs a higher base
revisit_triggers: overtime availability is cut
the worker's tolerance for off-hours shifts changes

base.update_signal: shift availability, overtime policy, or seasonal demand changes

nodes.definition: Rank the channels that actually fill local wage jobs: a personal referral from someone already inside (highest conversion), staffing/temp-to-hire agencies that hold standing orders with processors and warehouses, the CalJOBS portal and Stanislaus America's Job Center, and direct walk-in/onsite application at plant HR windows. Effort should follow conversion rate, not convenience.

pros.claim: A current-employee referral skips the resume pile and often jumps to onboarding
pros.example: a cousin on the dairy line hands HR a name and the worker interviews the same week

cons.claim: Staffing agencies take a margin and may keep the worker temp longer than promised, delaying direct-hire raises
cons.example: a 'temp-to-hire in 90 days' that quietly extends to keep the markup

failure_modes: pouring effort into generic online boards that local plants ignore
not asking everyone in the worker's network who is already employed locally
acceptance_tests: the four channels are ranked by conversion with a concrete next action for the top two given the worker's target sectors
revisit_triggers: a referral source appears or dries up
an agency relationship sours or a job center program opens

base.update_signal: a hiring channel's availability or conversion changes

nodes.definition: Assemble the minimal application that converts: a one-page plain resume listing recent jobs, dates, and concrete duties; a reliable phone number and voicemail the worker actually answers; references who will pick up; and readiness to complete an on-the-spot paper or kiosk application. For wage jobs, reachability and showing up beat polish.

pros.claim: A reachable phone with a working voicemail captures callbacks that otherwise vanish
pros.example: an employer leaves one message; a full mailbox loses the offer to the next applicant

cons.claim: Over-polishing a resume for hourly roles wastes time HR spends on it for about six seconds
cons.example: a two-page designed resume for a packaging job that the kiosk form ignores anyway

failure_modes: a voicemail box that is full or not set up
listing references who will not answer or vouch
acceptance_tests: a one-page resume, a tested reachable phone/voicemail, and at least two confirmed references exist before applying
revisit_triggers: the phone number or references change
an employer requires a specific application format

base.update_signal: contact details or reference availability changes

nodes.definition: Build the compounding relational asset that lower-wage workers most underuse: a clean attendance and reliability record, a reputation as the dependable person, and a growing network of current employees willing to refer. Each kept job and good reference becomes the highest-conversion channel into the next, better job.

pros.claim: A reliability record and inside referrals convert at rates no cold application matches
pros.example: a perfect-attendance line worker is recommended by their lead for the higher-paid operator opening

cons.claim: Building reputation takes months, so it cannot be the only near-term channel
cons.example: a brand-new worker has no record yet and must still apply cold in week one

failure_modes: burning a reference by leaving a job badly or no-showing
never asking employed contacts to refer
acceptance_tests: the worker maintains an attendance/reliability record and has asked at least two locally employed contacts to refer or vouch
revisit_triggers: a reference relationship is gained or damaged
the worker enters a new employer where reputation must be rebuilt

base.update_signal: a reference relationship is gained, used, or damaged

nodes.definition: Prepare for the screening wage employers actually run: a pre-employment drug test (still common in processing and warehousing despite California cannabis law), a criminal background check governed by Ban-the-Box and Fair Chance rules, a physical or lift/agility test for heavy roles, and a forklift practical test. Knowing the sequence prevents a late-stage surprise from killing an otherwise won offer.

included: background check and Fair Chance timing

pros.claim: Anticipating the lift test lets a worker self-screen out of a role they would fail in week one
pros.example: knowing a 50-lb repetitive-lift standard before accepting a case-stacking job

cons.claim: Assuming every employer drug-tests can scare a qualified worker away from ones that no longer do
cons.example: self-rejecting from a warehouse that dropped pre-employment THC testing

failure_modes: a background-check surprise the worker could have explained up front under Fair Chance
failing a physical that the role description hinted at
acceptance_tests: the worker knows, for each target role, whether to expect a drug test, background check, physical/lift test, and forklift practical, and has prepared for each that applies
revisit_triggers: an employer changes its screening policy
the worker's record or physical condition changes

base.update_signal: an employer's screening requirements change

nodes.definition: Separate the headline hourly wage from true take-home value: employer-paid health/dental, retirement match, paid sick and vacation, predictable hours, and reimbursed costs, minus payroll taxes and commute cost. It also contrasts a W-2 offer (taxes withheld, benefits, protections) with a 1099 offer (higher headline rate but self-employment tax, no benefits, and no overtime), which usually nets less than it looks.

pros.claim: Valuing employer health coverage can reverse the ranking of two offers with similar hourly rates
pros.example: a $1/hr-lower job with family medical beating a slightly higher cash-only one

cons.claim: Total-comp math is uncertain because benefit usage and tax situations vary per worker
cons.example: retirement match worth little to someone who cannot afford to contribute

failure_modes: taking a 1099 'higher rate' without subtracting self-employment tax and lost overtime
ignoring a long commute that eats the wage difference
acceptance_tests: each offer is reduced to an estimated net value including benefits, taxes, and commute, and any 1099 offer is compared on a net basis to its W-2 equivalent
revisit_triggers: a benefit plan or tax situation changes
commute distance or cost changes

base.update_signal: an offer's benefits, tax treatment, or commute cost changes

nodes.definition: Map the internal climb most processors and warehouses offer: line worker to lead to operator to maintenance/supervisor, each step gated by tenure, reliability, and a cheap stacked cert. Becoming the dependable person who learns the next machine and stacks forklift, food-safety, and basic maintenance credentials is the most reliable wage growth available to an incumbent.

pros.claim: Internal promotion preserves seniority and benefits while raising pay, beating job-hopping at the bottom
pros.example: a reliable packer trained on the labeler becomes a line lead within a year

cons.claim: Some employers cap internal raises so the only real jump requires leaving
cons.example: a plant where leads top out below what a competitor pays new operators

failure_modes: waiting passively for promotion instead of asking and cross-training
stacking certs the employer does not reward
acceptance_tests: the internal ladder for the worker's target employer/sector is mapped with the cert or behavior gating each step
revisit_triggers: the worker reaches a step or hits an internal pay cap
the employer changes its promotion criteria

base.update_signal: the internal ladder or its gating criteria change

nodes.definition: Cover the structured higher-wage routes outside a single private employer: union grocery/warehouse/health jobs with bargained scales and benefits, city of Turlock and Stanislaus County public-sector roles with defined pay steps and pensions, and registered apprenticeships (maintenance, building trades' non-driving paths) that pay while training. These trade a slower entry for durable, schedule-defined wage growth.

pros.claim: A public-sector or union ladder gives transparent step raises and a pension a private line job rarely matches
pros.example: a county maintenance worker on a published step schedule with CalPERS

cons.claim: These routes have slow, competitive entry and may require a clean record or a waitlist
cons.example: a county opening that posts twice a year and draws hundreds of applicants

failure_modes: missing a narrow public-sector application window
ignoring union or apprenticeship intake because it posts on a separate site
acceptance_tests: at least one union, one public-sector, and one apprenticeship route reachable from the worker's profile is identified with its entry requirement
revisit_triggers: a public-sector or apprenticeship intake window opens
a union organizes a local employer

base.update_signal: a public-sector, union, or apprenticeship intake changes

nodes.definition: Screen out dead-end, exploitative, and outright scam offers: any demand to pay for a job, equipment, or training fee up front; cash-only roles that skip I-9 and enable wage theft and no overtime; fake staffing fronts that collect personal data; and roles with no posted wage, no real address, or pressure to start without paperwork. The rule is no money up front and no work without a lawful I-9 and a stated wage.

excluded: legitimate union dues or licensing fees

pros.claim: A simple no-money-up-front rule eliminates the most common job scam in one stroke
pros.example: walking away the moment a 'recruiter' asks for a $200 onboarding fee

cons.claim: An over-aggressive filter can reject a legitimate role with a lawful licensing or equipment cost
cons.example: refusing a security job that lawfully requires a state guard card fee

failure_modes: accepting cash-only pay that later proves to be wage theft with no recourse
handing over SSN and bank details to a fake staffing front
acceptance_tests: the offer passes a go/no-go check: no up-front payment demand, a lawful I-9 process, a stated wage, and a verifiable employer/address
revisit_triggers: a new scam pattern appears locally
an offer trips a red-flag rule

base.update_signal: a new local scam or exploitative pattern is observed

nodes.definition: Assemble a dated 6-12 month income plan that sequences the chosen moves: secure earn-now bridge income, complete the highest-ROI short credential, shift to a premium-rich or higher-band role, and target a named promotion or union/public step — each with a milestone date and an expected wage at that date. The plan turns the scattered options into one ordered path.

pros.claim: A dated sequence converts a pile of options into a path with measurable checkpoints
pros.example: earn-now by week 2, forklift cert by month 2, operator band by month 5, lead by month 10

cons.claim: A fixed plan can ossify and ignore a better opportunity that appears mid-stream
cons.example: sticking to the cert plan when a referral opens a higher-band role this week

failure_modes: milestones with no dates so nothing is actually tracked
sequencing a credential before the bridge income that funds it
acceptance_tests: the plan lists at least four dated milestones in order with an expected wage at each, consistent with the worker's constraints
revisit_triggers: a milestone is hit, missed, or slips
a better opportunity appears that reorders the sequence

base.update_signal: a milestone is reached or missed, or the option set changes

nodes.definition: Define the loop that keeps the plan alive: a fixed reassessment cadence (e.g., monthly check-ins against milestone dates and pay) plus material-change triggers — job loss, a new credential earned, a constraint resolved, a wage-data update — that send the worker back through SELF_INVENTORY and PAY_BANDS to re-plan. Without this loop the plan silently goes stale.

included: re-entry into inventory and pay bands

pros.claim: A scheduled review catches a stalled milestone before months are lost
pros.example: a month-3 check shows the cert never started and reorders the plan immediately

cons.claim: Too-frequent reassessment churns the plan and prevents any single play from maturing
cons.example: rewriting the whole path every week so no credential is ever finished

failure_modes: no cadence set so the plan is never revisited
ignoring a material-change trigger and pursuing a now-invalid plan
acceptance_tests: a reassessment cadence and an explicit list of material-change triggers exist, each routing back to SELF_INVENTORY and PAY_BANDS
revisit_triggers: a material-change trigger fires
the cadence proves too frequent or too sparse

base.update_signal: a material-change trigger fires or the cadence is tuned

edges.why_related: the constraint filter is built directly from the raw inventory of hours, transport, and documents
constraints are intersected against the local sector set to decide which jobs are reachable
document readiness is first surfaced in the inventory and then resolved against I-9 lists
pay bands are estimated per role family within the mapped local sectors
the legal pay floor is read alongside the estimated bands to flag underpayment
the reliability record and referral network are built only once the worker is inside a first job
the references named in the application seed the referral network that compounds
knowing the legal floor is what lets the scam filter detect wage-theft and below-floor offers
fast-entry roles are drawn only from the reachable set the constraint model produces
entry roles are chosen with knowledge of which pay the least so the worker is not anchored low
short credentials are selected by which higher pay band they unlock
ROI is computed for each candidate credential's wage delta against its cost and time
the wage delta in the ROI calculation comes from the pay-band gap the credential bridges
premiums are computed on top of the base bands to find effective pay
which premium shifts are even keepable depends on the worker's hour and transport constraints
channels are prioritized for the reachable target jobs the constraint model defines
each sector posts through different channels, so the map informs where to apply
the minimal application packet is tailored to the top-ranked channels
the screening to expect follows from the channel and employer the worker is pursuing
physical limits and record details from the inventory determine which screens are a risk
total compensation starts from the headline band and then adds benefits and subtracts costs
premium earnings are part of the total-comp picture being compared across offers
internal promotion steps are gated by the stacked short certs
the internal ladder shape depends on the employer type within the sector map
which union, public, and apprenticeship routes exist is read off the local sector map
the wage advantage of union/public routes is judged against the private-sector bands
the scam filter screens the fast-entry offers most exposed to predatory hiring
a lawful I-9 process is the core test the scam filter applies
the earn-now bridge job is the first milestone in the dated plan
the highest-ROI credential becomes a scheduled milestone in the plan
a named promotion target is a later milestone in the plan
a union/public/apprenticeship step can be the durable end-state milestone
milestones are ranked by net value, not headline wage, using the total-comp view
only offers that clear the scam filter are allowed into the plan
the reassessment loop watches the plan's milestones and triggers re-planning
a material change sends the worker back to re-run the inventory
a wage-data update re-runs the pay-band estimate that the plan depends on
time and energy spent holding a fast-entry job competes with time needed to complete a credential
edges.resolution_rule: keep the earn-now job for cash flow but protect a fixed weekly block for the credential whenever payback is under ~2 months; drop the credential only if it starves rent

edges.why_related: chasing maximal overtime/graveyard hours can crowd out the cross-training that earns promotion
edges.resolution_rule: when a promotion step is within ~3 months, cap voluntary overtime to preserve cross-training time; otherwise bank the premium hours

edges.why_related: earning a high-ROI stacked credential causally opens the next internal promotion step

conflict_axes.name: earn_now_vs_invest_to_earn_more
conflict_axes.description: Immediate cash from a low-barrier job competes with time and money invested in credentials that pay later.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: secure bridge income first, then protect a fixed weekly block for the highest-ROI short credential

conflict_axes.name: premium_hours_vs_health_and_advancement
conflict_axes.description: Overtime and graveyard premiums raise pay now but erode sleep, family time, and the energy needed to cross-train for promotion.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: bank premiums when no near promotion exists; cap them when a promotion step is within reach

conflict_axes.name: private_speed_vs_public_durability
conflict_axes.description: Private processing/warehouse jobs hire fast but cap pay; union and public-sector routes pay more durably but enter slowly and competitively.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: run both in parallel — private cash flow now, public/union applications kept live

conflict_axes.name: headline_wage_vs_total_compensation
conflict_axes.description: A higher posted hourly rate can net less than a lower one once benefits, taxes, overtime eligibility, and commute are counted.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: rank offers on estimated net value including benefits and commute, not the posted number

conflict_axes.name: w2_protections_vs_1099_headline
conflict_axes.description: 1099 offers a higher headline rate but loses overtime, benefits, and protections and adds self-employment tax.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: compare on a net basis; default to W-2 unless the 1099 net clearly and reliably exceeds it

conflict_axes.name: narrow_reachable_vs_unblock_constraint
conflict_axes.description: Searching only within today's reachable set is fast but small; spending effort to remove a binding constraint widens it but delays earning.
poles: invest to unblock the binding constraint
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: unblock only the single highest-leverage constraint; otherwise search what is reachable today

conflict_axes.name: convenient_channel_vs_high_conversion_channel
conflict_axes.description: Online boards are convenient but convert poorly for local plants; referrals and walk-ins convert best but take social effort.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: spend effort proportional to conversion — referrals and agencies first

conflict_axes.name: polish_vs_reachability
conflict_axes.description: Time spent polishing a resume competes with the reachability and follow-through that actually win hourly jobs.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the resume to one plain page and invest the saved time in a reachable phone and references

conflict_axes.name: plan_stability_vs_opportunism
conflict_axes.description: A fixed dated plan gives discipline but can blind the worker to a better opportunity that appears mid-stream.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let the reassessment loop, not impulse, decide whether a new opportunity reorders the plan

edge_cases.description: Worker's I-9 document is expired or lost and surfaces only at onboarding
edge_cases.trigger: onboarding paperwork requested before a valid document set is in hand
edge_cases.mitigation: order replacements before applying and confirm a complete List A or List B+C pair physically in hand

edge_cases.description: Posted 'up to' wage is actually the rare 90th-percentile figure, not a starting rate
edge_cases.trigger: an attractive posting quotes a single high number with no range
edge_cases.mitigation: anchor expectations to the OEWS median for the occupation, not the advertised ceiling

edge_cases.description: Temp-to-hire conversion is quietly delayed past the promised period to keep the agency margin
edge_cases.trigger: the stated 90-day conversion lapses with no direct-hire offer
edge_cases.mitigation: get the conversion terms in writing and treat a missed date as a trigger to apply directly or elsewhere

edge_cases.description: Pre-employment drug test fails on a substance legal off-duty in California
edge_cases.trigger: employer still runs THC pre-employment testing despite state law
edge_cases.mitigation: know each employer's policy in advance and target the many that have dropped pre-employment THC testing

edge_cases.description: Background check surprises both worker and employer late in the process
edge_cases.trigger: a Fair Chance background check runs after a conditional offer
edge_cases.mitigation: know your record, prepare an explanation, and invoke Fair Chance individualized-assessment rights

edge_cases.description: Physical or lift test fails in week one for a heavy role taken without checking
edge_cases.trigger: a case-stacking or sanitation role with an undisclosed lift standard
edge_cases.mitigation: ask the lift/agility standard before accepting and screen it against the worker's physical limits

edge_cases.description: Cash-only job turns into wage theft with unpaid overtime and no recourse
edge_cases.trigger: an employer offers cash pay and skips the I-9
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse work without a lawful I-9 and a stated wage; cash-only with no paperwork is a no-go

edge_cases.description: Recruiter demands an up-front fee for a job, training, or equipment
edge_cases.trigger: any request for money before the first paycheck
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the no-money-up-front rule and walk away immediately

edge_cases.description: Seasonal pack-house furlough ends income every winter for a worker who treated it as permanent
edge_cases.trigger: the post-harvest slowdown lays off seasonal labor
edge_cases.mitigation: plan a year-round bridge or a credentialed move before the off-season, not after

edge_cases.description: Worker over-invests in a private forklift card the host employer re-tests anyway
edge_cases.trigger: paying a private school for a cert the employer does not accept
edge_cases.mitigation: confirm which cert the target employer accepts and prefer free WIOA-funded training

edge_cases.description: Plan never revisited so a stalled credential milestone goes unnoticed for months
edge_cases.mitigation: set a fixed monthly check against milestone dates and pay

edge_cases.description: A higher-paying referral appears mid-plan and tempts an unstructured pivot
edge_cases.trigger: a network contact offers a better-band role during an active plan
edge_cases.mitigation: route the opportunity through the reassessment loop to decide if it reorders the plan rather than pivoting on impulse

workflow.action: Inventory skills, documents, hours, transport, and constraints
workflow.description: Produce an honest record of what the worker brings and what limits them
workflow.gate: five+ skills, an hour window, a transport radius, and in-hand I-9 documents are recorded

workflow.action: Map dominant local sectors and employer types
workflow.description: List the real Turlock/Stanislaus sectors and example employers
workflow.gate: six+ sectors with two+ employer types each are named

workflow.action: Confirm a valid Form I-9 document set
workflow.description: Verify a List A or List B+C combination is ready before applying
workflow.gate: a complete unexpired document set is physically in hand

workflow.description: Intersect constraints with sectors and name the top unblocker
workflow.gate: reachable and blocked lists exist and the single highest-leverage unblocker is named

workflow.action: Estimate OEWS-keyed pay bands and flag the higher payers
workflow.description: Reason low/median/high bands per role family from the Modesto MSA method
workflow.gate: each role family has a reasoned band and the higher-paying families are identified

workflow.action: Select an earn-now low-barrier role and channel
workflow.description: Pick a no-credential reachable role placeable within weeks
workflow.gate: three+ no-credential roles with a one-to-two-week channel are named

workflow.action: Choose short credentials and compute their ROI
workflow.description: Rank short certs by payback against cost, time, and demand
workflow.gate: each candidate has a payback period and a go/no-go verdict

workflow.action: Rank hiring channels and assemble the minimal application
workflow.description: Order referral/staffing/job-center/walk-in and build the packet
workflow.gate: top two channels have a concrete next action and a reachable contact packet exists

workflow.action: Prepare for the expected pre-hire screening
workflow.description: Anticipate drug test, background, physical, and forklift practical
workflow.gate: the applicable screens are known and prepared for per target role

workflow.action: Screen offers for scams and dead ends
workflow.description: Apply the go/no-go red-flag rule to every offer
workflow.gate: no offer with up-front fees, no I-9, or no stated wage advances

workflow.action: Assemble the dated 6-12 month income plan
workflow.description: Sequence earn-now, credential, premium move, and promotion target with dates
workflow.gate: four+ dated milestones with expected wages exist in order

workflow.action: Set the reassessment cadence and triggers
workflow.description: Define monthly review and material-change triggers back into inventory and pay bands
workflow.gate: a cadence and an explicit trigger list routing to SELF_INVENTORY and PAY_BANDS exist

dominance_rules.rule: Legal work authorization dominates every job choice
dominance_rules.rationale: no lawful job can begin without a valid I-9, so document readiness gates all else
dominance_rules.action: block progress until a valid List A or List B+C set is in hand

dominance_rules.rule: Scam/no-go screen dominates any attractive offer
dominance_rules.rationale: a single exploitative offer can cost more than several good jobs earn
dominance_rules.trigger: an offer arrives with up-front fees, cash-only pay, or no I-9
dominance_rules.action: reject it regardless of the headline wage

dominance_rules.rule: Bridge income dominates credential investment when rent is at risk
dominance_rules.rationale: credentials only pay off if the worker survives the training period
dominance_rules.trigger: no stable income while a credential is unfinished
dominance_rules.action: secure earn-now work before committing unpaid training time

dominance_rules.rationale: a high-paying job the worker cannot physically keep yields zero
dominance_rules.trigger: a high-band role conflicts with hours, transport, or physical limits
dominance_rules.action: drop or defer the role until the binding constraint is removed

dominance_rules.rule: Net total compensation dominates headline wage in offer ranking
dominance_rules.rationale: benefits, taxes, overtime eligibility, and commute can reverse a raw-rate ranking
dominance_rules.trigger: two offers compared on posted hourly rate alone
dominance_rules.action: re-rank on estimated net value before deciding

dominance_rules.rule: Highest-conversion channel dominates the most convenient one
dominance_rules.rationale: effort should track callback odds, not ease of clicking
dominance_rules.action: spend it on referrals and agencies before generic boards

dominance_rules.rule: The reassessment loop dominates impulse pivots
dominance_rules.rationale: structured review prevents abandoning a maturing play for a shiny distraction
dominance_rules.trigger: a tempting new opportunity appears mid-plan
dominance_rules.action: evaluate it through the reassessment loop, not on impulse

dominance_rules.rule: Demand durability dominates raw ROI for a credential
dominance_rules.rationale: a high wage delta is worthless if the unlocked role has no steady local demand
dominance_rules.trigger: a credential shows high ROI for a thin-demand role
dominance_rules.action: discount its ROI by demand durability before scheduling it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm I-9 documents before applying, not at onboarding
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a winning offer collapsing on day one for missing or expired paperwork

anti_rework_rules.rule: Anchor pay expectations to OEWS medians before negotiating or accepting
anti_rework_rules.prevents: anchoring on a 90th-percentile posting and re-deciding after disappointment

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build the constraint filter before searching listings
anti_rework_rules.prevents: interviewing for jobs the worker cannot physically keep

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm which credential the target employer accepts before paying for training
anti_rework_rules.prevents: buying a non-transferable cert the employer re-tests or rejects

anti_rework_rules.rule: Secure bridge income before starting unpaid training
anti_rework_rules.prevents: abandoning a credential midway when rent forces a return to any job

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run scam screening before sharing SSN or bank details
anti_rework_rules.prevents: identity theft and wasted effort on fake staffing fronts

anti_rework_rules.rule: Get temp-to-hire conversion terms in writing up front
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an indefinite temp markup and a delayed direct-hire raise

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the reassessment cadence when the plan is written, not later
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a stalled milestone going unnoticed for months and lost income

iteration_protocol.trigger: the worker loses or leaves a job
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the inventory and constraint filter and re-enter at fast entry

iteration_protocol.trigger: a binding constraint is resolved (transport, childcare, document)
iteration_protocol.action: rebuild the reachable set and re-evaluate higher-band options

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new OEWS/EDD wage release or local wage-floor change lands
iteration_protocol.action: re-estimate pay bands and re-rank the plan's milestones
update reachable roles, recompute ROI of further certs, and advance the ladder

iteration_protocol.trigger: a public-sector, union, or apprenticeship intake window opens
iteration_protocol.action: apply in parallel and re-rank the plan toward the durable route

iteration_protocol.trigger: an offer trips a scam or exploitation red flag
iteration_protocol.action: reject it and re-screen the remaining offers

iteration_protocol.trigger: a milestone date slips or is hit
iteration_protocol.action: run the monthly reassessment and adjust the dated sequence

priority_rationale: Foundational inventory, sector mapping, and document readiness precede the market and search work because every downstream choice depends on knowing the worker's reachable set, the local pay structure, and a lawful I-9; synthesis and the reassessment loop come last because they compose the upstream outputs into a dated, self-correcting plan.
